families.topic: future cold risk, unequal vulnerability and cold-related mortality, morbidity and adaptation
families.page_title: Health Effects of Climate Change (HECC) report: cold
evidence_points: Warmer winters are expected, but cold weather and colder winters are predicted to continue.
Risks from moderate cold are expected to remain even as extreme-cold risk changes.
Cold-related deaths may initially rise because of population ageing before declining later in the century.
Older people, young children, pregnant people, people with underlying conditions and people in poor housing can be at higher risk.
Cold is associated with heart attacks, strokes, chest infections, influenza and falls.
Cold weather is also linked to anxiety, depression and excess deaths, many of which are preventable.
